# aeneid-012 review (Aeneid II.287–385), two passes

Findings: **major 7, medium 16, low 17** (40 changed, all by script; `t`, `ln`, `p` and the `l` line counts untouched, checked against the original) plus the refused/left items below. Speech marks checked unit by unit: every “ and ” in `t` is matched in `l` and `i` of the same unit.

## Changes
Major
1. u57 (382) n: 'visu' called "an ablative supine"; it is the ablative of the noun 'visus' (cause). Fixed.
2. u18 (322) n: 'Panthu' vocative claim ("Pantho or Panthe" for a Latin 2nd decl.) was wrong ('Pantho' is not what Latin would give). Now: Greek vocative in -u; a Latin -us noun would have -e.
3. u32 (345–346) n: 'audierit' tense claim ("poetic freedom in sequence") was false; a characteristic/result clause may take the perfect subjunctive after a past tense. Reworded, causal sense kept.
4. u32 n: nothing said 346 is a half-line. Added (Greenough prints it as a hemistich).
5. u16 (317) n: 'pulchrum' glossed "with est left out, mori the subject" while 'succurrit' is the verb; the infinitive phrase 'pulchrum mori' is the subject of 'succurrit'. Fixed.
6. u54 (376) n: 'neque enim… dabantur' glossed "for neither were answers"; it is 'for… not'. Fixed (and i "He finished" to "He had spoken", low).
7. About: "no hand could have saved the citadel if one could have" (garbled, reversed Hector's point). Now "if any hand could have saved the citadel, this one would have".

Medium
8. scan-fixes 2.310: 'Deiphobi' has four syllables (Greek Dēiphobos); scanner's one-syllable Dei gave a long 'pho'. Hand scansion added.
9. scan-fixes 2.339: scanner split Greek eu in 'Rhipeus' (Rhi-pe-us) and made final -us long before 'et'. Hand scansion: Rhi-peus as a spondee pair (see "left" for the one unverified quantity).
10. scan-fixes 2.366: 'soli' (sōlī) long-long, not short-long-short; scanner had to split 'Teucri' (Te-u-cri) to compensate. Hand scansion added.
11. scan-fixes 2.379: 'inprovisum' has long pro and vi; 'veluti' short ve, lu; scanner had them reversed. Hand scansion added.
12. scan-fixes 2.342–345: carrier lines of the half-line unit (scanner right; entries needed because the unit with 2.346 gets no sc otherwise, as in 2.232). 2.346 added as a "Half-line" entry (2 feet, one ×).
13. Iliad cites removed or made non-numeric (could not be verified from a public-domain reference reachable here): u8 "Iliad 11 and 14", u11 "Iliad 3.148", u40 "Iliad 16.156 ff.", u56 "Iliad 3.33–35". Each now says only that Homer has the comparable scene.
14. u0 (287) n: 'moratur' "puts off with an answer" (wrong sense; it is 'detain'). Fixed.
15. u8 n: 'praecipitis' stated flatly as accusative with 'silvas'; softened (it may be the torrent's epithet).
16. u23 (326) n: 'Argos' called "neuter plural accusative"; now just the place to which, no preposition.
17. u24 (327) n: 'incensa urbe' called an "ablative of place" (the Latin has 'in urbe'). Fixed.
18. u32 l: "would not listen to" (audierit is perfect, not conditional). Now "did not hear", still five lines.
19. u34 l: 'audentem' hung on 'desire' ("a fixed desire daring the last things"); now "me daring the last things", word order kept.
20. u33 l: "daring in battles to go" (invented 'go'). Now "to dare for battles".
21. u31 i: 'oblati' attached to Epytus alone; it covers Epytus, Hypanis and Dymas. Fixed.
22. u38 (354) i: "The only safety left to the beaten is to hope for none" is a known echo of the standard English line. Rephrased: "For men defeated there is one hope of safety: to look for none."
23. u43 (361) i: "set out the carnage of that night" echoed; now "Who, by telling, could lay out the slaughter of that night, who its deaths, or match its sufferings with tears?"

Low
24. u0 n: "ghost of the last unit's dream" clarified.
25. u7 (303) i/n: "by the ladder" (not in the Latin) to "by climbing"; 'ascensu' not "a stair or ladder".
26. u11 (311) i/n: 'proxumus' i now "the next house, Ucalegon's, is ablaze"; metonymy sentence tidied.
27. u15 (315) n: 'bello' dative softened (ablative possible).
28. u17 (318) l: 'Achivom' rendered "Danaans's"; now "Achaeans'". n: invented "no servant" removed.
29. u25 (328–329) i: "mixes fires in with fires" to "stirs the fires together".
30. u28 (333) i: 'stricta' attached to the point; now the steel edge stands drawn.
31. u30 (337) n: 'vocat' "nearest subject" to "singular with a run of subjects".
32. u40 (356) n: 'faucibus siccis' "quality or absolute" to "description".
33. u42 (360) n: "night as a bird of ill omen" (unsupported) to "winged thing".
34. u45 (365) l: "gods's" to "gods'".
35. u46 (366) n: 'sanguine' "ablative of price" to "of means".
36. u49 (371) n: 'credens' "accusative-and-infinitive left out" muddle clarified.
37. u54 i: see 6.
38. u10 (310) n: Deiphobus "Helen's third husband" tradition dropped.
39. u23 i: "cruel hand of Jupiter" ('hand' not in the Latin) removed.
40. u33 n: garbled "Greenough's 'audere' is followed here" sentence repaired.

## Refused / left
- **2.288 gemitus** (scanner cost 0.6): scanner fits it with 'ge', 'mi' long, which are short by nature; I could not construct a line with true quantities without assuming 'imo' has a long first i or a lengthened 'ter', neither confirmable from a public-domain prosody here. Scanner's fit (a valid hexameter) left. Not added.
- **2.325 Dardaniae** (cost 1.2): scanner splits 'ae' (a-e) and reads 'Troes' as one syllable; likely wrong in both, but I could not settle the true scansion (fuimus, Troes, fuit) with certainty. Left, flagged for the owner.
- **2.339 Rhi-**: the fix rests on 'Rhī' being long (the only way the line scans if 'peus' is one syllable); I could not confirm the length of that i from a reference. Medium confidence.
- **2.361** (COSTLY 2.0): hand scan Quis clā | dem īl-lī | us nōc | tis quis | fū-ne-ra | fan-do; every quantity checks. Scanner right; no entry.
- 2.340 Epytus, 2.341 adglomerant/Coroebus, 2.348 incipio/Iuvenes, 2.297 aeternum, 2.338 aethera, 2.326 Teucrorum, 2.383 Inruimus, 2.384, 2.289 Heu/ait: hand-checked, scanner right. 2.290 Troia = Tro-ja, 2.318 Panthus (long u) accepted.
- General limit: the scanner has no word-by-word vowel lengths, so lines it fits cheaply may still carry wrong quantities (audio uses them). I checked the lines the packet flags and the categories named in the runbook, not every vowel in every line.
- u40 ends at a comma after a long simile period: acceptable per the brief; left.
- u31 "line 426" for Rhipeus's justice is Virgil's own later line; kept.
- Glossary: not touched (glosser's job; gloss.json absent).

## scan-fixes.json entries added
2.310, 2.339, 2.342, 2.343, 2.344, 2.345, 2.346 (Half-line), 2.366, 2.379. Format checked against build_aeneid.py (letters of each `sc` string equal the line's words) and the validator's foot, syllable and × rules (all pass; 2.346 uses the half-line branch).
